messages:
maria-l: sec-bot alerted — sudden 1m spike in KMS.Decrypt errors for prod-serving-role, threshold 200 -> 1.1k. Looks anomalous, opening command room.
sec-bot: automated alert: metric=kms.decrypt_errors, env=prod, window=60s, value=1123, baseline=18. link: https://metrics/reports/1913456789
alex-c: on it. Maria, can you confirm if this correlates with deploys or RBAC changes?
maria-l: no deploys in the last hour per deploy-bot. RBAC audit doesn't show org-level binds yet, but running query now.
jamie-infra: pulling KMS audit logs and sysflow. running: ``query audit_logs where resource="projects/redwood/kms" and proto.method_name:"Decrypt" | sort desc | limit 50``
jamie-infra: quick skim — many Decrypt calls from svc-account:ci-runner@redwood with different targets, started ~00:52 UTC. Some calls show error: PERMISSION_DENIED then later OK.
olivia_sre: that pattern could be a credential rotation flapping or a compromised CI token. Suggest immediate containment: disable CI service account keys and add egress block for those pods.
alex-c: agreed. Taking these actions: 1) disable CI SA key id=ci-2026-09 2) add network deny for 10.34.0.0/16 -> kms endpoints (temporary) 3) create incident label in KMS console to prevent auto-rotation. I'll run commands and paste outputs.
jamie-infra: while Alex does that, I'm checking IAM binding changes: ``gcloud iam audit log query --filter='protoPayload.methodName="SetIamPolicy"' --limit=20`` — nothing unusual in last 24h. Also checking who created the ci-runner key: ``audit_logs where proto.method_name="CreateKey" and subject:"ci-runner"`` — created 2024-11-03 by pipeline@infra.
maria-l: interesting — maybe a leaked CI token. Alex, any failures when disabling the key?
alex-c: disabled key ci-2026-09, applied egress deny on kube-ns=ci-runner. Confirming KMS calls dropping now. Monitoring...
sec-bot: metric update: kms.decrypt_errors -> 78 (rolling down).
jamie-infra: starting token revocation for CI runners and rotating any remaining long-lived keys. Also adding a quick audit query for role.grants: ``audit_logs where protoPayload.serviceData.policyDelta.bindingDeltas.member contains "ci-runner"``
maria-l: we should also check RBAC on ephemeral controller service accounts — list recent RoleBinding changes: ``kubectl get rolebinding --all-namespaces -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.metadata.creationTimestamp > "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z")'`` — I'm running that now.
olivia_sre: ops team — notify product and security leadership, prepare customer comms if degradation persists. @oncall-comms can you draft a short note?
alex-c: status update: KMS decrypts mostly back to baseline, error rate ~12/min. CI-runner tokens revoked. Still seeing a handful of Decrypt calls from an unknown ephemeral SA: svc-ephem-42. Jamie, can you ID the pod/node?
jamie-infra: traced svc-ephem-42 to namespace batch-worker-prod on node gke-prod-node-12. Pod restarted 3x since 00:40. Logs show a job triggered by cronjob "bulk-embeds" — owner: data-eng/batch.
maria-l: paging data-eng on-call. @data-eng-oncall please confirm if bulk-embeds had a config change.
sec-bot: paging: @data-eng-oncall acknowledged incident #INC-2025-832, ETA 15m.
data-eng (external reply via page): investigating, we pushed a change to the bulk-embeds job last night to increase concurrency; no token changes intended. We'll audit container images and credentials.
olivia_sre: good. For now, keep CI SA disabled, block egress for batch-worker-prod to KMS until we confirm credential origin. Also create a read-only snapshot of KMS logs for forensic analysis.
jamie-infra: saved logs to gs://sec-forensics/1913456789/ and exported a subset: ``gsutil cp klogs.json gs://sec-forensics/1913456789/klogs.json`` — checksum: abc123.
maria-l: adding timeline notes: 00:52 UTC detection, 00:54 disable CI SA keys & egress deny, 01:05 identified svc-ephem-42 -> batch-worker-prod, 01:12 block egress for batch-worker-prod, 01:25 logs exported to forensics.
alex-c: quick vuln check — container image for bulk-embeds is from internal repo sha:7f9a — scanning now.
jamie-infra: scanning shows outdated kms-client lib in that image (v1.2.1) with a known bug causing retry behavior that could surface as multiple Decrypt requests when credential errors occur. Not a remote exploit but amplifies impact.
olmaria-l: note: add follow-up action to require kms-client v>=1.3.0 and add rate-limiter to job.
olivia_sre: assigning roles for this incident: Incident Commander: maria-l, KMS/Forensics Lead: jamie-infra, Containment Lead: alex-c, Communications: olivia_sre, Handoff to next shift: olivia_sre.
maria-l: agreed. We're stabilizing; prepping post-incident actions: rotate affected keys, enforce short-lived tokens for CI and batch jobs, add more RBAC alerts for unusual Decrypt volume, and add an automated deny-on-spike playbook.
alex-c: taking the action item to create the RBAC alert rule and short-lived token checklist.
jamie-infra: for handoff — I've uploaded evidence, queries, and a short runbook at https://wiki/internal/incidents/INC-2025-832. Key items: affected SA list, exported logs path, checksum, timeline.
olivia_sre: I'm taking 02:00 UTC handoff. Summary for next: containment applied, key revoked, egress blocked for batch-worker-prod, KMS errors near baseline, forensics dump ready. If anything regresses, escalate to sec-lead and consider org-wide token rotation.
maria-l: thank you team. Handoff notes appended. Closing action: formal postmortem scheduled 2025-01-08 16:00 UTC.
olivia_sre: picking up — acknowledged, will post a short incident update to #incidents and notify PMs. :white_check_mark:
